utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber apologises for the late start. We were dealing with some urgent issues in this case. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I was informed that you would like to address the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, with your leave, very briefly. Thank you. With your leave?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, last night, or rather this morning - late at night - we have finished completing a document, complementary document in relation to the report of Dr. Kovacs. I did not have time to copy this document but if you would like to have one copy, it is at the disposal of your Chamber and I can hand it to you now and we will make more copies later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the Prosecution already received a copy? In general, I would like to discuss matters once the parties have exchanged their views on the matter and not prior to that. That is just a matter of efficiency. So if the -- of course, I do understand, when I look at these papers, that I know what the subject would be. But I would rather first have the parties to exchange their views and then put in front of the Chamber what is in dispute and not do it by bits and pieces. Not because we don't want to hear about it; you might have noticed already yesterday that the Chamber is concerned about providing different copies of a document to the Defence, apart from the time it takes and I take that it has been considerable time. But if you prepared anything specifically on this issue, let's perhaps now spend two minutes on the main lines, but if the Prosecution has not been informed about what your position is, you want to tell the Chamber at this moment, we should keep it very brief because, otherwise, we have part of the discussion now, part of the discussion two hours, part of the discussion tomorrow morning, and I would rather concentrate. So if you would please explain very briefly what your position is. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, yes, gladly. The reason why I am doing it this way is only to facilitate the work of the Prosecution. The reason is that the motion has been done in French and nobody is able to grasp it immediately. And if I at least give its contents before the Chamber, the Prosecution will be able to know what it is about. The reason -- or the fact is, Mr. President, the Defence cannot accept documents that are false. I am saying documents that are false; not falsified documents, not fakes, but false documents. There is a very great distinction. Why, Mr. President? Because we discovered yesterday that there was -- chronologically there was something that seemed to be impossible. That is that the original of the document that was signed by Dr. Kovacs dates -- the date is 30th of April 2002. The translation of the document that we received is a translation, the one that was to be disclosed, was to be admitted, dates the 18th of February 2002. It is practically impossible - it is an oxymoron - it is impossible that a document which is dated 30th of April can be filed as a translation with a date of the 18th of February 2002. We discovered this only yesterday because we only received the original yesterday, but obviously this is a false document, and the Defence, that would like to save time, we cannot accept this. So, Mr. President, what we wanted to say is that in application of the Article 94 bis, there are deadlines that Prosecution has to respect. This has not been respected because the documents that were given to us, handed over to us, were not the right ones. So since these delays were not respected, we are asking for the application of Article 95, of Rule 95 and also asking the Prosecution why and how this happened. I hope that I was sufficiently brief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At least it is clear now for the Prosecution what you seek and what your main arguments are. I take it that the Prosecution will respond in due course. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, under the present circumstances, the Defence, having been provided with different copies of what -- well, different versions of the same document, I think the Prosecution was -- should seek whatever assistance they would need in order to understand a motion that has been drafted in one of the official languages of the Tribunal. So, I take it that the Defence will respond on short notice on the motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The Prosecution will, Mr. President, and might I express my concern as to what happened with the initial handing over of the Hungarian version. We also take it seriously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And we will make some enquiries on the issue which Mr. Piletta-Zanin has just raised. Thank you. Mr. President, whilst the witness is being brought in, might I have access to some exhibits. I have given notice of them. I would be grateful if I could simply have access to them to save time now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, and Madam Usher, could you please assist Mr. Ierace. Then, Madam Usher, would you please escort Mr. Karavelic into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Mr. Karavelic, may I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony. Please be seated. Please be seated. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Might the witness again be shown Exhibit P3728, that is, the maps. Examined by Mr. Ierace: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, General. Will you please go to incident 21, that is, the map marked "Incident 21." I think you have placed that map on the ELMO. Have you made changes to that map consistent with changes that you made to map number 13? In other words, you have moved the dark green line further east. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you made any other changes to that map?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go to the next map on which you have made changes. Is that map number 23?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it you made no changes to map number 22. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please point to the changes you made on map 23.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they similar to the changes you made on maps 13 and 21?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you made any other changes on that map?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go to the next map. What map is this, what number? Perhaps you can move the map to the right so we can see the number, and up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Yes, I see that. Please point to the changes you have made.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you moved part of the dark green line or the light green line?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A light green line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed on that map, is there only a light green line?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Effectively, have you moved the confrontation line, that is, part of the confrontation line from the northern side of the Miljacka river to the southern side?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you passed the line between two buildings which appear in a box marked "36" on the map?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any other changes to that map?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please go to the next map to which you have made changes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask you, Mr. Ierace, if we compare map number 24 with map number 5, it could be that that is due to the time frame, but on map 5, we see dark green lines as well where there are no dark green lines on 24. Could you please clarify that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please return to map number 5 and place that on the ELMO. Does map number 5 -- I withdraw that. On map number 5, you changed the position of part of the light green line. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And comparing that change to the change you made on map 24, the position is approximately - not exactly, but approximately - the same. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Map number 5 does show a dark green line. Is the -- given your evidence in relation to map number 5, I take it the dark green line is correctly positioned on map number 5. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that case, would you please change -- make the appropriate changes to the position of the dark green line on map number 5.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, map number 5 relates to June of 1993, and map number 24 relates to a period of time 12 months later, that is, June 1994. Were there any changes to that part of the confrontation lines between June 1993 and June 1994?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that being the case, clearly there should be a dark green line on map number 24, and in due course I will invite the Trial Chamber to assume that the dark green line on map number 5 should apply to map number 24 as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please now go to the next map --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since we are all here, perhaps it would be better if the witness did that himself and if he could mark that line on the map so that we would know that this is a line that he marked by his own hand and that this wasn't done by someone else. I think that this would be logical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I think the witness testified that there was no change. But let me just ask him. If you would look at map number 24 and if you would draw a dark green line, if you would have the instrument to do so, would you draw it the same as the corrected dark green line on map number 5?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, therefore, could you please then do that on map number 24.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the witness using a black marker? Blue. That's okay. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, on map number 24, just beneath the red circle, we see the word in English, "cemetery." It is shown by a white area. Yes, you now point to that area. Do you know what cemetery that was, and indeed, of course, is?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know a place in Sarajevo known as Hero Square?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does Hero Square appear on this map or not?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we go through the remainder of the maps, if you see it, would you please tell us. Please go to the next map on which you made changes. You are now on map number 26. Have you made changes similar to those made on maps of the same area, namely, have you moved the dark green line further to the east?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think for the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 25, can we have a -- no changes on 25 or? I then missed that. That is the same as -- yes, I see. It is the same as on 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think in fact we did skip 25 inadvertently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please go back to map 25. On both maps 25 and 26, have you made the same changes that you made to maps 13 and 21?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any changes to map 27?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please point to the change or changes.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is this change here when we are talking about the Strojorad facility. And on this map here, we have that square that I am indicating now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will come to the square in a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the change that you made on map 27 the same as the change you made on map 10 and others? In other words, you have made the same change earlier. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you please point to the position of Hero Square.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please place a circle, with a blue pen, around the square.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any stage between September 1992 and August 1994, did the 1st Corps have any facilities such as headquarters or armaments in Hero Square?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there was a company command there and a part of the battalion command during that entire period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know in which building or buildings those headquarters were?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In one of these buildings, on the ground floor or in the basement, but I am not able to point out the building precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many floors approximately, if you do not know exactly, did that building have?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The buildings are different but on average, it would be a building of 10 to 15 floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might the witness now be shown -- I withdraw that. Perhaps before I go to the remaining maps, Mr. President, there was an issue which came up yesterday. Would this be a convenient time to deal with that issue? I am happy to approach it in a different way. It involved yesterday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I do understand what you mean. Would it be suitable to discuss the matter in the presence of the witness or -- I mean, would it be appropriate?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What I have in mind is to ask a question which involves a different approach, and if that is objectionable, then, of course, we could discuss it in the absence of the witness, in order to save time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in order to save time, the Defence is not sure whether we understood. Is this about the claim stated by the Prosecutor, Mr. Ierace, yesterday about the perception of the geometry of what can be applied? Is this what we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would prefer the witness not to be present if Mr. Ierace, for the first time, formulates his question. May I ask Madam Usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom just for a very short time, I take it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, what question did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the subject of the next series of questions is the witness's knowledge of a notorious source of sniping fire in the area of Rajlovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we do it without using a map, indicating --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So maps will not be used where the answer to the question is indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I agree. But this witness had the opportunity of seeing the maps. He was able to remain here yesterday for 20 minutes, looking at them, and then there were these large triangles or rectangles in red marker regarding the direction of -- direction of sniper fire. It seems to me that he was already told what this is all about. So he had a lot of time to look at it. It is a little late. It should have been asked before he was asked to look at the maps. So, really, this is something that is unacceptable by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ierace, are you going to ask a question about a notorious sniper position that is indicated on one of the maps that the witness has seen?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Map number 16 and 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will not take the witness to the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that, but, Mr. Ierace, the Chamber has just conferred. If you ask the witness to go in detail through maps, indicating sniper spots, although you used the map for other reasons, the Chamber is not going to allow you to ask any question where you expect that the witness would have to locate something which was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. clearly indicated on the maps with the explanation of what it would be. So there is no problem in asking about the notorious sniper spot, but not those indicated on the map. Then you should have followed the other way and first asked about, without using the maps, but you can't give a witness a map with full detailed information of what you are going to ask him later on about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In that case, I won't take it any further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom. I take it that you meant on this subject, Mr. Ierace, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that while the witness was out, he took his briefcase, and returned with his briefcase. This is just to make sure that he did not consult any documents in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether that would be forbidden, but, I mean, if he spends overnight in his hotel room, he, I think, could consult as such whatever documents he has. But I will ask him, but I take it -- Mr. Karavelic, I take it that you took your suitcase and just in order not to lose it, but if you have consulted any documents, would you please tell us, when you were out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not look in my briefcase, and you can check to see, because there is nothing of the documents in the briefcase itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I always take proper care of my briefcase as well, I can tell you. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. In view of that last ruling, I might also return the exhibits that I had earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness now be shown Exhibit P3727.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we have it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am sorry, Mr. President. No. We will distribute those now. I think the Defence has a set.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe so. We will check. Thank you. No. Is this a map, Mr. Ierace -- or rather, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know yet what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To assist my learned colleagues, in the top right-hand corner, the number on the first map is 4014.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ierace, having had a very quick look at the map, I am aware -- could you please wait for one second, Madam Usher. Would you please take it. Just on the theoretical level, I am aware that you might run a similar risk as you did before. I just want you to clearly make up your mind on whether you would put yourself in a position that you couldn't ask certain questions not after you have shown documents to a witness. So I just want you to -- of course I do not know what questions you have in mind, but please be aware that a similar situation might arise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I understand your point, Mr. President. Would you allow me just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there are no anticipated questions, I think, that would revisit that same problem. Certainly not on the part of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then the document may be put on the ELMO for the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now in a similar fashion, General, would you look at the line that -- now I mean the green line.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Because of the scale, Mr. President, we do not have separate confrontation lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us whether the position of the green line correctly indicates the confrontation line on this map --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- for June 1993.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is just these two facilities here. This is when the lines stabilised and they remained more or less the same until the end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you indicate a similar change to ones you made on the earlier maps for the same area? Please take the blue pen and correct the line. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now move to the next map and advise us of the accuracy or otherwise of the confrontation line marked in green for July 1993.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could make a correction of the line here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed, would that be similar to the correction that you made on earlier maps of the same area?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the Trial Chamber, maps 16 and 17.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please make that change.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please move to the next map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, could you please take the witness back to the previous map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And perhaps first look at his corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is this, when I compare this with --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Map 6 was one of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, map 6. It is my recollection of map 6 that the dark green line would not be to the left of the two structures but would go through the two structures, to the right of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the light green line and here, we look -- but the whole front line now moved to -- I would say to the left of the four buildings where, on map 6, it is still in between.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, as best I can see on the screen, it seems to go over the top of the two buildings to the left of the parallel buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which is not the same as we see on map 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. There is a difference in scale. If one looks at map 6, of course the light green line was between the buildings, the dark green line to the right. I don't require that degree of precision in this map. But I am happy for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem is that the left -- on map 6, the left two buildings are, I would say, within the BiH positions, whatever the case may be. I mean, clearly they are within these positions, and that is not clear any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will clarify, Mr. President. Might the witness be shown -- please leave the present maps with the witness. Might the witness also be shown Exhibit P3728, in particular, map 6. On the top right-hand corner, numbers 3847 appear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, please compare the changes you have made to map 6 and the earlier map which is still on the ELMO, or was a minute ago. Do you intend there to be any difference in the position of the front lines, confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think there is any difference and perhaps it would have been better that I didn't make any changes in this map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "this map," do you mean map number 6 or do you mean the other map which has a --

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean this map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the record, that is map marked 1A, 1B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you saying that map 6 correctly reflects your memory of the position of the front line as of July 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: June 1993, the same?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you please go to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. President, might 3728 be returned, that is map number 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, would you please now move to the second map, that is the map which has a 4013 in the top right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We dealt with that. You wanted to move to the next one when I asked you to go to the previous one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry, General. Would you please now go to the map which has the 4012 in the top right-hand corner. On this map, having regard to the scale, we see a very large part of Sarajevo. Would you take your time to check the confrontation line in terms of its accuracy or otherwise as of January 1994. If I could assist you further with the request, would you please assume that the green line indicates the forward line of the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I mark in the changes?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would be the change.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go to the next map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps you could leave that one on the ELMO for a moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: It is okay now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please now go to the next map, which has the number 4011 in the top right-hand corner, and would you please check the accuracy of the green line indicating the forward line or front line for the 1st Corps as of February 1994.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I make the changes?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Just leave it there for a moment. Please now go to the last map, and that map has the number 4010 in the top right-hand corner. Please make any necessary changes to the indicated -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please make any changes necessary to the indicated forward line of the 1st Corps as of February 1994.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a change here, however, there are no significant facilities along the rest of the line. So, generally, I think that this -- this would be the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And indeed is the change that you have made consistent with the changes you made to three earlier maps in respect of the building you described as one which was uncompleted in its construction before the war?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the record, that is maps 4, 14 and 9. Might that exhibit be returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, in carrying out that exercise, we have effectively heard your evidence in relation to the positions of the confrontation lines in the area of the airport. And yesterday you indicated to us on a map the position of a tunnel under the airport. When did that tunnel start operating?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: August 1st, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I have your permission? In order that we are all able to follow what this is about perhaps we should ask Mr. Ierace if the map that we have in relation to incident 18 is an enlarged map 4010 which we saw a little while ago. So map number 8, is that only an enlarged version of the map that we looked at a little while ago which is numbered 4010? I am asking a technical question in order to save time because if that is so, then something is not quite right. May the Prosecution give us an answer to this, please. Mr. President, if you allow me, we would just like to save time, so I would just like to make a remark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the question is as follows: Is map number 2, which the witness saw a little while ago, is that a technical enlargement of the map that we saw a little while ago, which was numbered 10? So is it just an enlarged copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The English --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. President. That is my question. And if this is so, we can see that the lines are indicated differently and the title that we can read --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, of course it is not the same. On map 8, we find dark green lines and light green lines, while on 4010, we find only one line. So it certainly is not a magnified copy of that map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I wasn't speaking about the map that had information added to it, but about the map in itself. I am talking about the basic map. So I don't know whether we can be provided with this information or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, these are different cards. If, I, for example, may draw your attention to the word "Grdonj," on one map you find an indication what I take it to be the 8th and on the other one we find not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is there and the scale is the same, so it seems to me that this could be a photo enlargement. So on the map, on the line, there is an expression "seven woods" which is right below, and also a structure which resembles --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... so I am sorry for confusing. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The scale is the same, Mr. President. So I think this is an enlargement, and if this is so, we need to know this. So is this an enlarged map, and if it is so, I would just like to state that the light green line from map 8, the BH line, passes through a very different place from the line which can be seen on map number 5. Because above the words "seven woods" on map 8 -- on map 5, this is above and on map 8, it is below, this expression "seven woods." So we need to know a little more. So I apologise, but I had to intervene because I would like to know, in the technical sense, which map this is, whether it is enlarged or not. And if that is so, then we would like to know why these differences are taking place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... I take it it is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, is the understanding of the Chamber right that map 4010 is the same map which we find enlarged as map on which figures number 8, and that the confrontation lines are roughly drawn not making any distinction between BiH front lines and Serbian, but somewhere in between?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in answer to the first part of your question, it is the same map if I can exclude from that answer the position of the confrontation lines. This is an electronic map. Effectively, a computerised map, which one is able to reproduce in different scales. As to the second part of your question, Mr. President, the -- as indicated on map 5, the green line represents the position of the front lines, which is why I effectively corrected my first proposition to the witness and throughout the maps described the line as the 1st Corps front line. Now, I think I see the concern of my learned colleague, and I will make some enquiries about that, but perhaps the appropriate thing to do is to reshow the maps to the witness and invite his observations, if any. Naturally, the scale of map 5, that is 4010, is relatively large compared to map 8, and that might have led to some misunderstanding. But in any event, I am happy to do it now while it is fresh in everyone's mind. So if there is no further questions, Mr. President, if that is convenient?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, once again, in order to avoid a situation where we would have incorrect documents, I think that the technical data that I have, and I did learn to read a map a while ago, so this is the same. So we have 12.500 on this enlarged map and we have the same scale on this other map. So there is a technical issue here where we have scale indications which are seemingly incorrect. If we are reproducing something or enlarging something, then we need to say, "Don't pay attention to the scale," or we should be provided with the true scale. So this is the job of the Prosecution, not our job, so something is perhaps incorrect, something is wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This issue has been raised before. The parties have been invited to bring one map of which the scale was incontested, and of course, if you enlarge maps, the Chamber is well aware that the scale will not be valid any more. And I think we verified that on one or two maps, so that the Chamber is fully capable of extrapolating whatever needs to be extrapolated. Then, of course, apart from the scale, we do see that on map 4010 the confrontation lines are, I would say, more global and sometimes they seem to coincide with Serbian lines and others places a bit more with BiH lines. Is the Defence of the opinion that, having regard to the fact that we have detailed information on the other maps, that it should be corrected as well on 4010 or could we just accept that this is a rather global approach where we find a more precise approach in the other maps?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will consult with my colleagues. Give me just one moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If this is possible, Mr. President, we would like the witness to be more specific about map 4010 Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and to also mark all the changes or indications which would be required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, would you please ask the witness to indicate the difference between 4010 and the other maps. And the Chamber thinks it confusing if we would try to make other markings on the big map; if the witness would have indicated precise front line positions at the enlarged maps. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, with that in mind, might the witness be shown Exhibit 3727, in particular, map 4010; and Exhibit 3728, in particular, map number 8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I think you have in front of you at the moment the last map that you were shown, that is, 4010. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look now, please, when it is given to you, to a map which shows in greater detail an aspect of map 4010 and compare them, please. Please do not mark anything, but simply take your time to compare them and let us know when you have identified the relevant part on map 4010 of the area covered in map 8. Please do not mark anything.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This line should go below, under number 9056, because the line of defence is here, the line of defence of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in terms of understanding why you did not pick that up earlier, if you look at map 8, you see a number of roads indicated in yellow.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they of any assistance to you in determining the positions of the confrontation lines on that map? If you look at the other map, please, map 8.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Does that map show a lot of roads which don't appear on the larger map, that is 4010?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of the relevant part of the larger map, is there an absence of much detail?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, given the directive to not mark the larger map, does that suffice?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me ask you, Mr. Karavelic, if you look at the map 4010 where only one confrontation line or front line is given, in your view, is that line indicating approximately a combination of the split-up confrontation lines you find in more detail on map 8?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This line on map 4010 indicates the line of defence, of the defenders of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The defence. Would that be, in your view, the same as the light green line on map 8?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I think that's it, but on this map, 4010, the line should go under Trg 906.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if I then may ask your attention for other details. For example, if you look at map 8, the light green line goes through Sedam Suma and through this area below the words "Sedam Suma," where on the 4010 map, the line is clearly above the words "Sedam Suma." Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I said. I said that it would need to be placed a little more to the south and then it would come to that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not only at 905, I think it is, where it says "Grdonj," but the whole line should be a lit lower there. But on many other instances, it very much looks as if the line on 4010 is more corresponding with the dark green lines than with the light green lines, if I compare the two maps. For example, there were -- we have the words -- let me just try to find it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you permit me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you permit me to say, there is a part here which absolutely 100 per cent coincides here to the right from Trg point 906. There is a rectangle of streets where -- and this part is absolutely identical on both maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do agree with you, yes. I think it was a mistake I made. So you say that the only change that should be made is that, in the area of Sedam Suma, the line should be in accordance with the light green line as we find it on map 8. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are talking about the same time or has this line changed or -- Mr. Karavelic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace. Perhaps it is time for the break. We will adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hope the parties will accept that the Chamber spent not only the break but even the last 10 minutes on issues concerning this case and, unfortunately, you had to wait for 10 additional minutes. Mr. Ierace, would you please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the two exhibits in front of the witness might be returned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, are you aware whether civilians or BH armed forces personnel, or both, crossed the airport at night between September 1992 and the operation of the tunnel under the airport?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there both civilians and armed forces personnel who did that?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time of year 1992, until the tunnel under the airport was built, the crossing, or rather, running across the airport runway, 99 per cent of the people who did that were civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the other 1 per cent, the armed forces personnel, I take it, crossed the runway at night?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were individual examples of command staff who did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the civilians, were there attempts by the BH authorities to stop them or some of them from leaving the city?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is not about -- it wasn't about stopping the people, preventing them from leaving the city, it was more about preventing the civilians from crossing the runway because of the casualties that were sustained on the runway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which forces or force was responsible for civilian casualties on the airport at night?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Troops of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, which kept lines on both sides of the airport runway; on the beginning and the other end of the airport runway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in the interests of the BH authorities to prevent civilians from leaving the city in 1992, 1993, and 1994?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This question should perhaps be divided as to what we already know and what I do not wish to bring up here before the witness. The period seems to me quite large just to be included in one question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that is so, you can ask for further specification. The question as such is not inadmissible. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, could you please respond to that question.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never asked that I should prevent the people from leaving out -- leaving the city at any price, however, there was a school of thought among the people, among some people, that if it was allowed that all the civilians population should leave the city, or the majority leave -- would leave the city, then the city itself would fall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If that had happened, that is, that all the civilians or the majority of the civilians were either permitted to leave the city or indeed required to leave the city, was there anywhere they could go?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the population of the city, say, in mid-1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number. I think that the figures go from 250.000 to 350.000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the civilian population of the city, say in mid-1993, include refugees from other areas of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you received training in the JNA in the early years of your military career. What was the -- was there any similarity or connection between the doctrine of the JNA and the military doctrine which applied to the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the 1st Corps, when formed and during the war, based on JNA doctrine or on some other doctrine or on no other doctrine?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout 1992, I could say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We would have wanted to know which 1st Corps are we talking about, because there were two 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would have thought that was abundantly clear from the examination-in-chief so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace. I think there could be no confusion, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. So perhaps you could consider next time to refrain from interventions when there is no risk of any confusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will rephrase the question. Was the doctrine of the 1st Corps based on JNA doctrine in terms of its structure, its disciplinary proceedings and so on?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout 1992, most of 1993, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as corps commander, under the JNA doctrine, if you wished to discipline a subordinate, what options did you have available to you? What action could you take under that doctrine?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a corps commander, I had the possibility of using discipline punishment which will include up to 30 days in detention. Then I had the possibility of sending the offenders, that is, those who committed these offences, possibility of sending them to the discipline -- court of discipline. That is, I had the possibility of sending them away, of this offender, from their establishment duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you became the corps commander, I think you said effectively from August 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was written, I think, on the 20th of July 1993 and I took over the duty only about the end of August or the first days of September 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on assuming the position of corps commander, were you aware of certain disciplinary problems with any of your brigades?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which brigades they were.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less serious problems I had with the 9th and 10th Brigade, which were located in Stari Grad, in the Old Town. And with other units, but it is true, a lot fewer problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the 9th and 10th Brigades, can you give us some understanding of the nature of those problems that existed when you assumed command of the corps? What type of problems?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was about refusing to obey orders, by the commander of the 10th Brigade and the deputy commander of the 9th Motorised Brigade, and also them not carrying out orders by the commanders and also not following the guidelines and the instructions given by the corps commander and by the corps command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How important did you think it to obtain authority to exert your authority over those brigades?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this to be a very important matter. Without it, it is absurd doing anything else as a corps commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What steps did you take at first, if any, to exert your authority, to bring them into line? I don't want a lot of detail, we don't have much time, but if you could tell us the type of actions, if any, that you took.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This problem dated probably from the spring of 1993. After taking over the duty of the commander of the 1st Corps of the arm of BH, that very same moment I asked verbally and in writing, I asked the commander of the Main Staff and the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina that I should tidy up the situation in the corps and to bring them into a normal situation, and that the two commanders of the brigades should be subordinate to my commands, to my orders. It was only after about a month or perhaps month and a half that there was political agreement, and I was given the possibility to even use armed force to do this, which is what I did on the 26th and 27th of October, 1993 when the commander of the 10th Mountain Brigade was executed, and a number of people, some 100 or several hundreds of people were detained, and I think about 200 people or 100 people were tried.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you told us yesterday that your training included training in the military academy in Belgrade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said you did some additional training. I think you used the words, "officer training," is that correct, in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of your training include training as to the requirements of an officer, the courses to be taken, the strategies to be adopted by an officer if that officer has insubordinate subordinates, in other words, subordinates who will not follow orders?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every officer who is educated through a training programme in the JNA, in most of the literature and the books that are in the curriculum, it is said that the Geneva Conventions, among others, should be respected. And through the training and throughout the career of any officer, it is so stressed, it is underlined how important it is to protect and defend civilians in any conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate that. But did your training include what obligations you have to bring subordinates who are out of control, so as to speak, into line?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the training and education include the options available to a general, if the general is unable to exert discipline over subordinates who are engaged in unlawful acts or refusing to follow orders?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the rules of the JNA, a commander - that is, if commander is a general - must ensure preconditions within his area of responsibility in relation to the defence, and he has to put everything under his control, under his command. Otherwise, there is a possibility of him being taken off his duty, his post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you had failed to bring the 9th and 10th Brigades under your command and control, even after the use of force, what remaining option or options would you have had as the corps commander?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only option I had left was to leave my post, leave my duty, which is what I even suggested to my commander-in-chief and to the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that the papers appointing you as corps commander were dated late July and that you assumed the post in early August and that you attempted peacefully to bring them under your control, and finally, you used force against the aberrant brigades. When did the operation which involved the use of force against them conclude?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 27th of October, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during your period as deputy commander and later commander of the 1st Corps, did you become aware of allegations that mortars were being fired from the grounds of Kosevo Hospital and from the precinct of the United Nations field headquarters at the PTT building?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any enquiries as to whether any units or forces of the 1st Corps were responsible for that?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were forces or units of the 1st Corps responsible for that?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This could not be officially confirmed ever by UNPROFOR, nor was I able, in the course of my investigations, ever to come to that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did -- to be clear on this, did you ever order or do you know whether anyone else in the 1st Corps ever ordered that such activities take place?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I responsibility state no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, General, in relation to cars, that is private cars in Sarajevo, firstly, in 1992, that is between September and December 1992, did you observe civilians to be driving their cars in the city?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1993, at some stage -- I withdraw that. Did that continue throughout 1993 or not?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This continued during the entire period from 1992 to 1995, but as time went on, there were fewer and fewer vehicles, and, therefore, the civilians moved around much less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From where did the civilians, especially as the war wore on, developed, obtain fuel for their private vehicles?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government of Bosnia-Herzegovina had the fuel and the biggest user, the 1st Corps, or the army, the headquarters of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, also the MUP, special purpose industries and possibly some other units that used the fuel. They were the biggest users. The civilian population could get fuel by buying it across from the line of separation, and in various other ways within the city itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say, "by buying it across the line of separation," do you mean buying it from territory controlled by the Serb forces or not?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that an officially sanctioned means of obtaining fuel or was that part of what is sometimes called a "black market"?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was something that was sanctioned, but at the same time, officially or unofficially, there was a black market.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Sarajevo I think there was a predominance of Volkswagen Golf motor vehicles. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just interfere. Could the word "sanctioning" create any confusion?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, did the BH authorities, that is the government, approve civilians in the city trading with individuals on the territory controlled by the Serb forces? In other words, did the government approve Sarajevans trading across the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the instructions that I received, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, was the most popular car in the city the Golf?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the most popular and it was the most numerous vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is still is, is that correct? There were Golfs everywhere?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is still the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the army also use Golfs, apart from other vehicles?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What fuels were the Golfs able to operate on?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, we were in the most difficult situation regarding all kinds of issues, but amongst other things also because of fuel. Due to shortages, we used oil from the transformer stations to fuel our vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just going back to an earlier issue: Up until October 1993 when you brought the 9th and 10th Brigades under your command and control, effective command and control, were you able to enter their area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean after that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the summer, until the 26th of October 1993, I couldn't nor the commander who was on duty before me, nor anyone from the 1st Corps command was able to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the names of the two commanders of the brigades?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the 10th Mountain Brigade was Musan Topalovic, called Caco, and the deputy commander of the 9th Motorised Brigade was Ramiz Delalic, called Celo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the commander of the 10th Mountain Brigade known also as Cace?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, General, do you know whether General Galic received the same training that you did in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that that is so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, with your permission, I will begin with the cross-examination and my colleague will continue. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karavelic, good day.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, can you confirm for us that on the 21st and the 27th of November 2001 [sic], you provided a statement to investigators from the Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I gave one statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the 21st and the 27th of November 2000?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the dates exactly, but it was in the autumn of the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us that on the 22nd and the 23rd of October, 2001, and the 31st of October and the 2nd of November 2001, you spoke with investigators Hogan and Richard Philipps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karavelic. Do you confirm that the statements that I have just mentioned were read to you or you read them and signed them?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karavelic, yesterday at the beginning of the examination-in-chief, you said that after a brief period you attended the military academy and after citing some information about your career, you said that you deserted from the JNA in December 1991 when you held the rank of captain first class.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then, when you had that rank, did you expect to receive a higher rank?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what rank and what was required for you to receive this rank?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the condition to be awarded the rank of major was to take an exam and to spend at least four years as captain first class, so on condition that you also received an official grade of a "particularly exceeds" or "with merit." Since I started to attend the course in 1989 for major and I spent four years with the rank of captain first class and in Zenica my brigade commander, Colonel Tomislav Sipcic, once we moved from Ljubljana, in August 1991, I did receive this grade, "exceptionally exceeds."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you say this grade "exceptionally exceeds," was a certain grade required also when you were taking the major's exam?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the grade which you received for that exam?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven point something. I don't know what the average mark was for that exam. That is not so important. The important thing is to pass the exam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, you said that you passed with a seven, and if the Defence tells you that it was actually a six, would you agree with that, that you received a grade six?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, I see that you -- yes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... nodding before and the transcript cannot record any nodding. So your answer is no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has a document, a certificate from the high military schools where you can see that Mr. Karavelic graduated with a satisfactory grade, a six.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the average but there is also a tactical, a work, a thesis. So this is what is really important, the thesis on defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karavelic. You told us that when you deserted in 1991, that you joined the Patriotic League. Is this true?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, can you tell us when the Patriotic League was formed?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several sources. The most official source, or actually the most official date is the 10th of June 1991, in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 10th of June 1991, is that the same month when the congress of Muslim intellectuals was held at the militia building?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that when you became a member of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't even know about it then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a professional soldier, could you please tell us whether the forming of the Patriotic League was practically the formation of the party army of the SDA political party?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what to respond to that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were members of the Patriotic League persons who had weapons, who were armed?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From late 1991 and early 1992, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us that the Patriotic League was a kind of Pan-Islamic paramilitary organisation in the years 1990 and 1991?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a legitimate military force in 1990 and 1991?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the overall military and political situation in Yugoslavia, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, according to the constitution and the laws that were in force, was not the legitimate military force the JNA, which was comprised by the Yugoslav People's Army and the TO?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we will agree that the Patriotic League was a paramilitary organisation.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because the JNA and the TO had lost this legitimacy that you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, when did the JNA lose this legitimacy?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The moment when I was in Zenica, in the month of September 1991, where I was the commander of the Motorised A Battalion, which I brought from Ljubljana.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, would you agree with me that the JNA -- well, that this is your personal opinion and that, in accordance with the law and the constitution, the JNA was a legitimate military force?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the law and the constitution, yes, on condition that it -- that they are respected by everybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, can you please tell us when you became a member of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The moment that I left the Yugoslav People's Army, I asked for work. I was looking for a job, and so I happened to at that point join the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the Patriotic League in the month of February 1992 had about 60 to 70.000 armed members and this was confirmed at the meeting at Mehurici near Travnik?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you thinking about the entire Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very difficult to believe that this was the actual number, that the Patriotic League had so many members. If it did, then the outcome of the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina would have been different. But even if such figures are being talked about, then this would include all possible kinds of weapons, all kinds of hunting weapons, handguns and so on, so perhaps that would bring us to a number which seems quite big.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, when I asked you this question --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, having regard to the question and the answer, there is either a translation problem or a misunderstanding on the part of the witness. Either way, some clarification is needed. The question was about, as I understand the translation, membership; the answer was about weaponry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it needs no clarification because the question was about the membership of armed people. I see on page 43, line 18, at about 60 to 70.000 armed members. So weaponry is relevant. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, when I put this question to you, perhaps I should have asked you first whether you knew that Mr. Sefer Halilovic wrote a book, "Cunning Strategy"?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in your time as deputy commander of the 1st Sarajevo Corps, could you please tell us what was the function of Mr. Sefer Halilovic in the BH army?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From late May and early June 1992, when Sefer became the commander or the chief of the General Staff of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, so the number one man, and he stayed in that post until the spring of 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I understood, you said the General Staff. Did you mean the General Staff or the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it changed names frequently. The Main Staff or the General Staff, but that is what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I put the question to you about the number of the armed members of the Patriotic League, I had in mind the book written by Mr. Sefer Halilovic and this number, this figure, comes from that book.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this would then apply from the 6th -- to the 6th or the 7th of February.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your post in the Patriotic League when you joined that organisation? Did you receive any kind of special function?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From mid-January 1992, I was appointed commander or coordinator of the Patriotic League for the Tuzla region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say, "commander of the Patriotic League for the Tuzla region," are you saying that you were actually the commander of the Tuzla Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once Bosnia-Herzegovina was recognised as a sovereign state on the 6th of April, the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 8th of April re-named the old Territorial Defence into a new Territorial Defence and then I think that on the 10th of April, I was appointed commander of the regional headquarters of Territorial Defence in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, in that period, was there a division or did the Territorial Defence in the area of Bosnia-Herzegovina divide? And when I am talking about this division, I am thinking of this in ethnic terms.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't call it a division. I would say that there was a complete privatisation of the Territorial Defence by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, isn't it true that the division of the TO along ethnic lines did take place and that the SDA party was the one that, through the Patriotic League, appropriated all the TO weapons in places where the Muslims were in a majority?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this did not happen and I cannot agree with that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I respectfully object to, again, double-barreled questions or triple-barreled questions. The last question was in fact two separate questions and it leads to confusion if the witness does not address each one specifically but rather gives a general answer. I don't suggest that it necessarily happened on this occasion, but it does happen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
