utterances.text: Yes, it is advisable in general to split up. If you ask a confirmation of a certain -- but sometimes it is acceptable, in order to save time, to combine a few issues. But as soon as the witness says that he couldn't confirm it, then you have to split it up anyhow. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, you told us that as the commander of the TO of Tuzla region, you were captured on the 22nd of April 1992.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understood that you said that in the period from this 27th of April until the 11th of May, 1992, you were tried. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that there was a trial going on against you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether then in 1992 on the territory of Yugoslavia there were military courts that were active, that were authorised to try army members?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean Yugoslavia or Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time when I was captured, on the 27th of April when I was captured, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia brought its constitution, adopted its constitution and legally and formally the dissolution of the former Yugoslavia ended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that you were tried, and I believe that in your statement of the 22nd and 23rd of October you said that you were sentenced to death, that you were sentenced to be executed by being shot. Can you tell us which military court, which court sentenced you to be shot?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer because I had no contacts with anyone except with three colonels. They can answer this question, from Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether you were sentenced to be shot or not.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that at the end of the trial, I was asked in a direct question, "How would you like to be executed?" And my answer was, "Just to have the bullet."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, during the 12 days that you spent, as you say, in Sremska Mitrovica, the court, the relevant military court, did they actually have trial proceedings ongoing against you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question. Nobody talked to me except in an office three times a day. There were three colonels who were sitting -- who were sitting on a bench.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly, as a soldier, you know that there is such a thing as military security?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you interrogated by the members of military security?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may have been members of military security. It could have been a court-martial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Mr. Karavelic, then, in 1992, military courts functioned in Yugoslavia and they were the only ones that were authorised, that were competent to hold trials and to bring verdicts for military personnel.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question. I do not know what formally the situation was in Yugoslavia, whether it was at war or it wasn't at war, whether there were some war regulations that were adopted or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that Yugoslavia was not at war at the time, and that the military courts functioned normally and worked, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree with a legal interpretation by an official expert.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that there was no trial proceedings going on against you, and that you spoke a falsehood when you said that you were sentenced to death, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I didn't say that I was sentenced to death. I just told you what they asked me, and that brings me to think this, because I was told that I would most probably be shot. These three colonels told me that. I -- my intention is not to mislead. If this is not an important question, then we can go to other questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, you said in your statement that you were sentenced to be shot.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get a sentence?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was told verbally what I had already told you. Because following this, I was transferred to Belgrade, and then from Belgrade by helicopter to Pale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm to us that, considering that the soldiers that were killed in Tuzla at the time, their soldiers of the JNA, could you confirm that you were captured and that you were then transferred to Sremska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was captured, including some officers from my staff. I was not alone. And what the motives were, what the reasons were, that is a slightly larger question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, you will agree with me that there were no trial proceedings conducted against you, that this was a question in investigative procedures and that you were captured as a prisoner of war. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Two objections, Mr. President. Firstly, this is the fourth time the witness is being asked whether or not he was tried; and secondly, this whole issue has now taken I think some 10 minutes and is of no relevance to the issues before the Trial Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the first objection is sustained. The question has been put several times to the witness and the witness has given answers and it has become quite clear what the difference of view is. Ms. Pilipovic, if you would bring in any new element in this respect, you may put additional questions to the witness. But if it is all about the same, then please proceed to your next subject.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction, line 49.16, instead of "captured," it should be "exchanged."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While the Defence was preparing for the cross-examination of Karavelic, Mr. Karavelic said in his statement that he was sentenced to be shot by execution, executed by shooting and the Defence asked for documents from military court in Belgrade, which was the regular military court, which confirmed that Mr. Karavelic was never detained or was never in detention, that he was never remanded in custody in the military court. That is the reason why the Defence wished for Mr. Karavelic to be precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There is no need. I mean, until now, you have put all the questions in this respect to the witness and we heard his answers. And the point is quite clear, so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to provide the certificate of the military court in Belgrade as a Defence exhibit. We have a sufficient number of copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I would be grateful if my learned colleague could indicate the date on which this document was disclosed to the Defence, pursuant to Rule 67(C).

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence was not able to disclose this document in a timely fashion to my learned colleagues, considering that we were in The Hague at the trial. My associates, at my request, managed to get hold of this certificate. This is a certificate which confirms that there were no proceedings conducted against Mr. Karavelic, that he was not detained, and that he was not remanded in custody in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the question is when it was disclosed. When did you receive the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we are now on the 18th, if I am correct. We have heard several times serious complaints that not documents available have been immediately disclosed to the -- to you as Defence. And you complained when it was the day before, or even the morning. I now see that you have this document for six days. You said on the 12th of July. You would like to respond?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it was issued in Belgrade on the 12th of July. I did not receive it immediately. That is the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question to you was: When did you receive the document and your answer, according to the transcript, but it might be a mistake, was, "Your Honour, on the 12th of July." So I took that as a starting point. But whatever could be said about it, certainly during the last break or this morning or yesterday evening, you could have done so. And as you know, we have always taken very seriously if you as Defence, were not properly informed. Let's try to prevent that a similar situation will --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... for the future. Mr. Ierace, very often you responded that the document was very short. This is a very short document. So if you would need more time, please let us know. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, on the 11th of May, 1992, when you were exchanged, you said yesterday during the examination-in-chief that you took some time to recuperate. Could you tell us when did you join as active military officer, when did you join the BH army?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was exchanged on the 13th of May in Sarajevo in Lukavica, at the petrol station between the airport and Stupska Petlja, and after a short period of recuperation, just by joining and be appointed as the department of the regional staff of the Territorial Defence Staff of Tuzla, that is how I joined the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, when did you arrive in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was exchanged, on the 13th of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that then you continued to be military active in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After about a month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "after about a month," could you perhaps tell us when and where did you again become an active military officer of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The very same moment I was included in the original staff of the Territorial Defence because I was exchanged upon the request of the members of the Presidency, of BH Presidency, and then Ministry of Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you are saying is that from the end of May, you were already active in the Territorial Defence of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say a little bit later, possibly from mid-June -- from early June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, how was the Territorial Defence in June organised in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance -- considering what I did, what I was able to see, what I was able to live through, then the commander of Territorial Defence was Hasan Efendic, although the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina issued decrees on activating and mobilising Territorial Defence. The establishment and the mobilising of Territorial Defence went with great difficulty, happened with great difficulty for the reasons that there were no files, there were no documents, that were taken away because all of the units of the Territorial Defence had been disbanded, were destroyed because of what you said, there was a division along the ethnic lines. And at that time, the main carrier, the main factor has to be said of the defence of Sarajevo was the Territorial Defence, and most of the work was done by the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, are you saying that the Territorial Defence, specifically talking about Sarajevo, was created from members of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The BH army was created from the Territorial Defence and from the Patriotic League, members thereof, but it could be said that at the time of the existence of the Territorial Defence still parallelly, there was the existence of the Patriotic League, although there was a decision of the Presidency of the BH which then the Patriotic League entered the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether there were any other units in 1992 that became part of the Territorial Defence apart from the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision actually says "all armed units"; that is, Green Berets, all other formations, HVO Croatian, Defence Council, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you said all armed units, you mentioned Green Berets, HVO, and the Patriotic League, that was in 1992. Could you tell us, what other units, specifically in Sarajevo, entered the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Units of the Territorial Defence that were managed to become established in any form, whether partially, only 50 per cent, under 50 per cent, then units of the Patriotic League which then also became units, Green Berets, HVO. I don't know whether you mean anything specific, that is what existed in Sarajevo. I don't know what else you want me to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, were there paramilitary formations, paramilitary units which existed in Sarajevo, like the military formation that -- under the control of Juka Prazina, of Musan Topalovic, Ramiz Delalic? There were all these paramilitary groups in Sarajevo in the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were units which had orders from the Ministry of Defence, from the Main Staff, and so on. They cannot be defined as being paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, how were they armed, these units?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A small number of handguns and, for the most part, hunting weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, could you tell us, when was the 1st Corps established in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the right date is the 1st September of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, I will show you a decision which units are to form part of the 1st Corps. This is --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a document that the Defence received from the Prosecution. But the Defence would -- before Mr. Karavelic is shown this document, the Defence would like if Mr. Karavelic can be shown document number 143.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, because you said that you had such a document. We had now time to read it, I take it Prosecution as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, do you see before you a certificate issued on the left-hand side by the military court in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you confirm to us that it is correct that what it says in the military certificate, that you, as a former captain first class of the military post called Tuzla throughout 1991 [as interpreted], you were never detained then or later, you were never remanded in custody in the military investigation prison in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was a translation issue, but my friend said throughout 1991. The document refers to 1992, not 1991. That is my first objection. The second is that I think the evidence of the witness was that he was sent to a prison in Sremska Mitrovica. That prison by name is not mentioned in the certificate, so I think there is a connection that should be made before she can go further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes Your Honour. The Defence is -- would like to have this document tendered because of the statement of Mr. Karavelic, because he said that the -- because of the statement of Mr. Karavelic, the only court which was competent to try military personnel was the military court in Belgrade. Considering that Mr. Karavelic said that he was sentenced to be shot, the Defence wanted to show that Mr. Karavelic is not speaking the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it, Ms. Pilipovic, that the first objection was either a mistake or a translation issue; 1991 and 1992. Yes. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1992, Your Honour. I think I said 1992. That's what it says in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the transcript it appears as 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to my friend's response, the certificate simply says that Mr. Karavelic has not been brought or detained in -- it is not even "the" or "a"; "in military investigating prison in Belgrade." The evidence of the witness is that he was taken to a prison in a particular place. There is not yet a connection in the evidence between military investigating prison in Belgrade and the named prison in the witness's evidence. And certainly no reference as to charges one way or the other, simply the certificate goes to whether he was brought or detained there. If I could spell it out, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that the evidence of the witness yesterday, Ms. Pilipovic, was: "On the 22nd of April 1992 --" and I am referring to page 11.769, line 11: "On the 26th of April 1992, I was captured and taken to Belgrade to the prison in Sremska Mitrovica." The next question was: "Were you tried?" The answer was: "From April 28th until the 11th of May, I was taken before three colonels every day, three colonels of the JNA, who processed me and at the end they told me, they asked me how I would like to be executed." That was the evidence given yesterday. I see that -- perhaps you have read the document. Of course, where the document comes from, you have not asked whether the witness has ever seen this document before. But, if you confront him with the information contained in it, perhaps literally, and perhaps put to him that the Defence is in the possession of a document which would say - although you mentioned that already before - and then perhaps ask his response to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, when you said that you were brought to Belgrade, could you confirm to us whether there was a -- whether there was a trial proceeding conducted against you in Belgrade? Were you tried in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Tuzla, Tuzla airport, I was placed in a Gazelle plane, I was taken to Banjica, to Belgrade, and there was a major who was holding a gun against me. When I arrived there, I was met by a colonel who was from the Air Force, he was in a blue uniform. I don't want to tell you about other things, what he did to me, because that is not what this case is about. But I was immediately placed in a vehicle, which was a van, which had no windows, and I was immediately taken to Sremska Mitrovica. On the 11th of May again, I was again brought to the same heliport in Banjica and with a helicopter I was taken to Pale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. Karavelic, you are confirming that while you were in Sremska Mitrovica, you were not processed, there were no trial proceedings against you, you were not sentenced?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm this to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have no translation at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this is time for a break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is. But after the witness answered, "I cannot confirm this to you," Ms. Pilipovic, did you say anything else other than that you thought it would be time for the break?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That is clear. We will adjourn until 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, before I continue with my questions, I would just like you to confirm whether you carried out criminal act by deserting from the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object on the rounds of relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, what is the relevance of whether you consider this a criminal act and perhaps have a lengthy legal discussion on --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in order not to go into a lengthy debate, the Defence will withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, you stated that in the month of May you came to the Main Staff, the main headquarters of the BH army. Can you tell us when that was in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 13th of May, when I was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, then, in May, was there an UNPROFOR presence in Sarajevo at that time?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes, because UNPROFOR came to Sarajevo on the 1st of April 1992, to Sarajevo and Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that sometime in the course of the month of May after the 12th of May negotiations were conducted so that the JNA could leave the barracks which, at that time, were surrounded by the Sarajevo TO? Do you know that such negotiations were conducted?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that some negotiations were conducted. I didn't participate in them. And at that time, I wasn't -- I wasn't present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But later during your tour of duty, was one of the conditions set by the TO regarding the departure from the Sarajevo Barracks, one, that the weapons at the disposal of the JNA should be left to the TO?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that, but I think that that was one of the wishes, the desires.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that there is information that a large quantity of arms did remain with the Sarajevo TO and that it was placed in the Marshal Tito and the Bubanj barracks, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present when --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: This is the third time that my learned colleague has referred to material which she has not shown to the witness. The first was a book, and the second was an account by someone else. It simply isn't probative to elicit evidence in this way, especially in this case, given that the witness has already said that he wasn't part of the negotiations. If my friend wishes simply say to him, "Do you know whether a large quantity of arms remained with the Sarajevo TO?" I would have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the subject is not in issue, but, Ms. Pilipovic, as you know, leading questions, and especially in cross-examination, are quite acceptable, but telling the witness what the sources are, where you have your information from, I think without confronting the witness with these sources is not the proper way of doing it. So would you please proceed and, again, the subject is no problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when I told Mr. Karavelic about the information from the book, I had the book before me and I could have shown it to Mr. Karavelic, but he confirmed that he knew about the book, and this book has also been disclosed to my learned friends Sefer Halilovic's book, "Cunning Strategy." As far as my questioning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection was only about the last question. There were no objections made before, although Mr. Ierace now makes reference too that he perhaps could have objected against it, but he did not. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, when I asked you about the quantities of arms of the JNA in Sarajevo, whether you knew anything about that, before that I asked you whether you knew whether UNPROFOR was present in Sarajevo at that time and you answered, "Yes."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your work as deputy commander in the corps, did you find out that a large quantity of arms was left to the TO? Did you have such information? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, my information is quite the opposite. So, which one is correct, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I told you that the Defence has a statement by Mr. Richard Gray who at that time was on duty in Sarajevo with the UNPROFOR --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Same objection, Mr. President, for the same reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, if you want to confront the witness with a specific source of information, then you perhaps put that information to the witness and ask questions about it. Also the Chamber has some difficulties in following who Mr. Gray is, what his document is about. So to understand the testimony better, I think if you want to use the material, that is no problem, but then you should do it so that everyone can see it or you just ask the question and do not refer to any specific source of your knowledge. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to the course my learned colleague proposes. The witness has clearly said his information was quite the opposite and he doesn't know where the truth lies. There is no probative value in showing the witness, against the background of that answer, a statement by someone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not know that, Mr. Ierace, because I -- let's just assume, although perhaps not probable, that Mr. Gray has put in his statement - we don't know that statement - that this witness would have told him in detail, that would pertain to the reliability of the witness. So I can't say that unless I have seen the material. So, therefore, if you want to confront the witness with the material, please do so, Ms. Pilipovic, but otherwise do not mention specific sources.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has Mr. Gray's statement, which was disclosed by the Prosecution. Specifically Mr. Gray says in his statement, he talks about the barracks and the weapons in Sarajevo on the 24th of May. And my question was put to Mr. Karavelic whether UNPROFOR was present and whether he had information about the weapons which remained in the barracks, which remained in the barracks and was handed to the TO when the JNA withdrew. This is why I wanted to mention Mr. Gray's statement, because at that time Mr. Karavelic was already in the Main Staff of the BH army and he must have some information about that and he probably wishes tell the truth. And this is the reason why I am telling him about the statement of Mr. Gray who states quite the opposite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... of Mr. Gray, but confront him with the relevant part of the statement of Mr. Gray.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, if I were to say to you that the forces of the TO blocked the barracks and requested that all the weapons held by the JNA be handed over to the TO, would you agree with me that this is correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I would agree with the fact that it was requested that all the arms in possession by the JNA in the barracks should be left behind, but I cannot agree with the fact that it was actually left behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, before the break I asked you about what you knew about the forming of the 1st Corps in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the rest of that question and the answer of the witness was, "Yes."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how many military formations and what were they that comprised the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we verify first. Mr. Karavelic, Ms. Pilipovic said to you before the break that she asked you about what you knew about the forming of the 1st Corps in Sarajevo. The interpreters could not hear your answer properly. Did you just answer "Yes" or did you add anything to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have a problem saying anything right now. I can respond to any question, that is no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am just --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the interpreters did not hear the end of Ms. Pilipovic's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am sorry. Ms. Pilipovic, I misunderstood the message from the interpreters. The last part of your question was not heard by the interpreters. Could you please repeat your question which started with: "Before the break I asked you about what you knew about the forming of the 1st Corps in Sarajevo," and what was then the last part of your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And which military formations comprised the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was one of those responsible when we are talking about the forming of the 1st Corps of the Army of BH and I was the deputy commander of that corps. Had this been requested of me, I could have brought documents, maps, to show the court here. But now I cannot tell you just off the top of my head exactly which units were part of the corps, although I can name some of them

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, allow me to show you a document that the Defence received from the Prosecution. It is a decision stating which units were part of the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And we would like to show this document to Mr. Karavelic so that he could confirm for us whether these were actually the units that comprised the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, do you recognise the document that you have in your hands?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that I recognise it because this is a document from the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This kind of document would come to the Main Staff and then, once it passed through the Main Staff, I would receive a document from my commander. So I did not have the opportunity to see a document like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, can you confirm for us that this document, which is in the form of a decision, states in item 3 under I, that: "The composition of the 1st Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina includes the following units."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think these are the units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, are you confirming that you can see, based on this document, that the composition of the 1st Corps of the BH army, dated the 18th of August, 1992, included 13 or 14 brigades and that is stated under "A"?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. And this is stated in the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the document states that the brigades, the 1st Independent Sarajevo Brigade, the Stari Grad Sarajevo Brigade, Zmaj Od of Bosnia, Centar Sarajevo, Hadzi Lojo Brigade, Stari Grad the 13th Brigade, New Sarajevo the 14th Brigade, Novi Grad the 15th Brigade, Novi Grad the 1st Dobrinja Brigade, the 1st Podrinje Brigade, the 2nd Podrinje Brigade, the 1st Sanjak [phoen], the 7th Brigade, the 1st Mixed Artillery Regiment, the 1st Infantry Brigade Igman, and also Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of these units did exist, most of them. I am not quite sure about the 7th Brigade as such. This is something I did not come across before. At the time the 1st Corps was formed, I don't see any detachments which would comprise the 1st Corps but which were there on the 1st of September, for example, the Sirokaca Detachment. When the 1st Corps was formed, these units were there. This document looks as if it was written later in November or December 1992. But --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm, in view of the role that you had in the Main Staff and later as the deputy commander of the 1st Corps, that these brigades did comprise the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The majority of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, can you tell us where the command posts of these brigades were located, the brigades that we see mentioned in this decision?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without consulting documents, it would be difficult. 1992 was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Mr. Karavelic, if it says, for example, under number 2, the 1st Brigade Stari Grad Sarajevo, would you be able to tell us where the Stari Grad Brigade was located, where the command post was?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you believe me if I told you that in the beginning, the commander was one person and that two or three people made up the command of the brigade and that they didn't have a specific location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, when you confirmed for us that these brigades made up the 1st Corps, could you also tell us, since you were the deputy commander of the 1st Corps --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The question misrepresents the witness's evidence. He said the majority made up the 1st Corps. The question suggests that he confirmed all of them were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the objection is sustained, but I would say that there was hardly any risk of confusion. I wouldn't say no risk, but hardly any risk. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, can you please tell us how the brigade members were trained --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: What kind of uniforms did the brigade members of the 1st corps have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Specifically during the whole of 1992, the 1st Corps had a minimum number of any kind of uniforms. And for the most part, the soldiers wore the clothes that they brought from home.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, you said that you didn't see that in this division, but that special units or special detachments were also part of the 1st Corps and you mentioned the Sirokaca special detachment.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the TO detachment of Sirokaca, not a special detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this detachment linked to the Siroka region of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in accordance with that principle, can you confirm that such detachments were formed in that way?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the beginning, the majority of the companies and the detachments were formed like that. Brigades were formed later. And the corps itself was formed from a large number of such detachments and from a smaller number of brigades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, can you confirm for us that the 1st Corps also comprised the reconnaissance and sabotage unit which was formed in the month of October, that it was formed and that it became part of the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you thinking of Juka Prazina's brigade?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I am not thinking of Juka Prazina's brigade but I am just asking you, was there an order to form a reconnaissance and sabotage unit?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think there was such an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which units made up the reconnaissance-sabotage brigade within the corps, initially?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reconnaissance-sabotage brigade which was formed did not ever achieve not even a quarter of the establishment brigade, the way it should look. But in the beginning, it was formed from, I think, personnel from platoons and companies of that kind in order to form such a brigade within the 1st Corps of the Bosnia-Herzegovina Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the units which made up the reconnaissance-sabotage battalion have any specific names, and if they did, did such -- which -- what were the names of those units?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't have any specific names, but I would have to go through the documents in order to see what the exact name of the brigade was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show Mr. Karavelic a document which it received from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace was on his feet after some hesitation, but yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Hesitation because, Mr. President, I think at page 69, around line 6, there was some part of Ms. Pilipovic's question, and perhaps an answer, that we did not have translated. It might have been around page 9 -- line 9, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will read for the witness because I have no proper recollection of that. But I will first ask my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi informs me that the microphone at a certain moment was closed but that whatever has been said has been repeated. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, you told me that if you saw the order, you would be able to tell us more about the reconnaissance-sabotage brigade of the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And Your Honour, the Defence would like to show Mr. Karavelic a document which the Prosecution disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please assist, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, do you recognise this document? Page 1 is in English and page 2 is in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it is an okay document. Whether I recognise it, it is a difficult question. I can start by saying that this is possibly correct. I am not doubting this document at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, from this order we can see that within the 1st Corps the reconnaissance-sabotage brigade was created and that it comprised special unit Sultan Fatih, special unit Boris, special unit Fatih, special unit Kobra, special unit Ljiljana, section for upkeep of materiel assets, special unit of the corps, and special unit Drago Prazina. Is this correct, Mr. Karavelic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these names are more or less known to me. I recognise them. That all these units became part of a sabotage reconnaissance brigade, that is something I cannot agree with because I am almost certain that they did not become part of it, not even half of them. Because order is one thing and it is a completely separate thing what at the time, at that very moment on the ground, in practice, could have been implemented.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, are you saying that all of these units are known to you and that they did exist at the time in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They probably are all units that existed in brigades, which is what I said a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you cannot confirm that they all became part of the sabotage reconnaissance brigade, are you saying that some of the units did not wish to become part of that brigade? Did they act independently?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not what I am saying. That frequently, the chief of the Main Staff would make a decision without looking at the situation realistically based on the information from local commanders and so on. Frequently, it occurred that there would be a decision made, an order issued, and then it would have to be revised when it was to be implemented.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, as a deputy commander of the 1st Corps, were you informed how these units were armed?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no difference in comparison to other units in terms of weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the document, it says, "special unit." Are you saying that they existed, too? Could you tell us what is the strength in terms of numbers of such units and where were they located, where were they billeted?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you a figure. I don't have it. But as far as the word "special" is concerned, I can only say that then, in 1992 in Sarajevo, it was very important for some people to call themselves "special units," and they wouldn't even amount to being the letter "S" of a special unit. And one example is Juka Prazina, who had such people with him, and he more or less insisted on calling himself a special unit, but there was no difference between them and any other units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you mentioned Juka Prazina, could you tell us how many people were members of that special unit under Juka Prazina?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were about a couple of hundred only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were they based? What offices, what premises did they use?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The actual commander of the brigade even had at one point its command post in the premises in the building of the Presidency of BH. But where the other units were, I cannot tell you now. The great frustration that the army felt in 1992 was this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, bearing in mind your background, your education, your military expertise, could you perhaps explain how can a special unit under the command of Juka Prazina - and the Defence does have data, information, that he was a criminal - how could its command post be in the building of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, again I object. It is inappropriate to put to a witness that sort of proposition. I have no objection to my friend putting to the witness that Juka Prazina was a criminal, or asking was he a criminal. Within the confines of procedure, that is acceptable. But to simply inform a witness that the Defence has information to that effect is not only not probative, but can lead to misunderstanding and distortion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic, I think there is no need to refer to any evidence, of course, unless you confront the witness with certain documents or, for example, convictions or whatever. And I have a second question: Do I have to understand that the special unit Drago Prazina, is that what you are referring to as the Juka Prazina -- no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then -- because what I -- you asked the witness how it would be possible that -- let me just try to re-find it. Yes. The testimony of the witness was that the actual commander of the brigade we are talking about had, at one point, his command post in the premises, in the building of the Presidency of the BH. You asked the witness to explain how it could be that Juka Prazina had its command post in the building of the Presidency, which is not the same. I am not saying that -- at least, it does not follow from the answer of the witness, but if you would say that the commander of the brigade was Juka Prazina, then first please ask the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Before we proceed, another matter. On two of the documents that have been shown to the witness together with translations, there are -- on each, there is a sentence which has not been translated. I think it appropriate that my learned colleague bring out the translation of those sentences. In the list of the brigades, it is the last sentence, and in the list of the special units --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first see what document are you talking about. D144, Mr. Ierace, or... ?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have difficulty in reading the numbers, the Defence exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 145.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but 144 precedes 145.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It must be -- I assume it's 144. It ends with ERN 214.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And what part is not translated?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if you look at the translation, it ends with B battalions, one independent battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then it's indicated that a part has not been translated by giving dots.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. And one can see there is a part of the order which has not been translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Also indicated by dots, if I am correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, and on the second document, it is point four which has not been translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was indicated by dots, isn't it? I see three dots under "special unit Drago Prazina." And do I understand that the documents are disclosed by the Prosecution and that the Defence considers the translated parts to be relevant? Is that what I understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it was disclosed by the Prosecution, but we had no prior notice that they were to be used today. Given that they are orders and that they are one-page orders, that is the parts not translated, part of the orders --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you think -- let's just try to find a practical solution. I do understand that the Defence does consider these altogether three lines on the two documents not relevant. I think that we are not finished with the cross-examination of the witness by today. Would the Prosecution find a possibility before tomorrow to have at least the content of these three lines, if not formally translated, at least that you know what it is about and whether it would be relevant in your view.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. President, to assist we will do that. But if there are documents to be shown tomorrow morning, might I respectfully submit that, when it is only a sentence, my friend could at least read it out so we can have the live translation from the booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it, Ms. Pilipovic, that if you would use a document by tomorrow, that translations have already been prepared. So if you would provide then the Prosecution with the numbers, and when translations were prepared by the Defence, for the translations as well by the end of the session.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Karavelic, my question regarding my question in relation to the document 145 and special units, did you tell me that these units were also special just like special units of Juka Prazina?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? What do you want me to say? I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You yourself, Mr. Karavelic, told me that these units had a special status just like the special status -- special units of Juka Prazina.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not tell you that. These units did not have the status like the units of Juka Prazina because it was directly linked to the chief of the Main Staff and these other units were on the level of the brigades and they became part of the 1st Corps. Juka Prazina's unit never became part of the 1st Corps, only later, when Juka Prazina was executed, it then became part of the 1st Corps. That was in much later, that was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you tell us that Mr. Juka Prazina was killed, that he was liquidated, could you tell us, what was his role in the BH army?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander of that brigade while he was in Sarajevo. He led troops into combat. He worked just like anyone else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Juka Prazina's brigade, was it part of the 1st Corps of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that it acted independently?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a unit linked, it was an independent unit directly linked to the Main Staff of the army of BH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are saying that it was under the direct command of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, in 1992 where were the positions of Juka Prazina's brigade in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am talking about 1992, September-October -- 1993.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that his brigade had anywhere permanent positions. It was a manoeuvring unit which was used for attempts of break-through and stopping that break-through, preventing the break-through.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "manoeuvring unit" could you perhaps tell us how many manoeuvring brigades were there within the 1st Corps, as part of the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That number went usually from one to two, depending on time. Occasionally there was one, sometimes there were two and this would depend on the assessment of the entire political and military situation in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, considering that we spoke of special units, could you tell us whether in the period of 1992 - we are talking about until September 1993 and 1994 - whether there was a special sniper unit in Sarajevo that was active?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special unit snipers in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Special unit called Seve.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was never in the 1st Corps, first of all. And this name is associated with MUP units and it is currently there are trial proceedings in relation to this in Sarajevo. What is all true in relation to this, I couldn't tell you, but certainly there was nothing under sniper unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Seva?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seva, yes, but there were no other prefixes attached to this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, could you tell us whether in the period while you were carrying out your duties in 1992, 1993 and 1994, whether Mr. Stjepan Siber also had certain duties in the BH army.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was the official deputy of the chief of the Main Staff, together with Mr. Jovo Divjak, as I told you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have contacts with him in the course of your work?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you informed by Mr. Siber that in May 1992, members of the TO in Sarajevo were distributed 540 sniper rifles from the Zrak factory?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, no, and this is the first time I hear anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge that Mr. Siber had written a book, a diary for 1992?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity of reading this book?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only partially, only in relation to myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that in this book, Mr. Siber is writing that in the month of May there were 540 rifles --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Firstly, the witness has said that he has never heard of it before, and, therefore, assuming that Mr. Siber's book claims that, it is of no probative value to suggest it to the witness. Secondly, if there is probative value to it, then the quote should be given to the witness, or at least a copy provided to the Defence [sic] while it is read to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, if you are confronting the witness with part of a book, unless the book as a whole has been disclosed to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Prosecution I should have said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Prosecution, yes, yes, and even then it would be appropriate to inform the Prosecution that you would rely on a certain page or certain part of that book. That is the first issue. The second issue is that the witness has answered the question that he hears it for the first time. I do not know what you are about to quote from the book, but if that would be just the same as you did already on page 78, line 23, about the distribution of sniper rifles to members of the TO, that would be repetitious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I just would like to inform the Chamber that part of the book that I asked Mr. Karavelic about is part of the Defence Exhibits, but because I wasn't precise enough, I will list it tomorrow, I will cite it tomorrow. I think it is 304, but I will do it tomorrow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I know that some parts of this book -- I don't know whether these are the same parts, but some parts of the book were tendered and admitted into evidence. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, any translation problems you would like to draw our attention to?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Unfortunately, many.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you could do it in such a way that everyone can follow it and nevertheless as short as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 67.26 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 8.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, could you say page so and so, line so and so, and then this word not translated or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, gladly. Page 6, line 16, "26" instead of "36." Page 26, line 16, "enlargement" is not what was needed because we were talking about the largest possible map. Page 33, line 10, the word "executed" should not be the same as "eliminated." I believe this was a military execution. Page 7 [as interpreted], line 14, we were talking about three colonels and the text is only talking about colonels, "the colonels." And then there is a problem in relation to a place name, page 51, line 4. Line 4, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before we adjourn, I would be grateful for an indication of how much further time will be allowed for the Defence for cross-examination. It would assist in terms of us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as I can see, the Prosecution took four hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that included a very large period of time devoted to marking maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Part of the marking of maps was done in court and, to some extent, I think the Chamber met the requests of the Prosecution to do it as efficiently as possible. But, of course, it is up to the Prosecution itself whether they want to spend time on marking maps. If a map has been produced by a witness at a prior stage of the investigations, that usually has been accepted. It depends on the circumstances, but a lot of marked maps have been -- have been used.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just in relation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Even if we take that into account, I think we spent approximately 20 minutes on starting to marking the maps. Then the maps were marked during the break, and most of the time was, as I indicated already yesterday, was spent by asking questions about the markings. The marking itself was of relatively -- took relatively short time. That was four hours altogether so even if there would be reason to deduct anything, until now, the Defence took 1 hour and 40 minutes. I don't know whether the Defence has any indication whether they would need the full four hours, if they would be granted --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am afraid that this should be a little bit more than four hours that the Prosecution has used, because I don't know whether you have used the break in this calculation, but this time was used by the witness, i.e., by the Defence to supervise him while he was marking. If this calculation was included, fine, but I don't think you did include it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I did not include it. I will consider with the Chamber whether it should be included, although it is not time used for examination of the witness, but of course the most important thing is whether it takes time in court. I mean, that is what we are talking about. At least it did not take time in court. I perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you hear me in response to what you have just said? Firstly, in relation to the estimate of four hours, our estimate of the entire time is 3 hours and 38 minutes. Secondly, you said a few minutes ago, effectively, that is something that should have been attended to by the Prosecution before the witness got into the witness box. I specifically sought your approval to do that the day before Mr. Karavelic entered the box on the morning, and you indicated that you would reflect on it and inform me later. That didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We did fail to do so and we then considered whether it would be appropriate or not. And it might have come a bit as a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. surprise to you that halfway we changed, but the Chamber first wanted to know what kind of markings and what kind of questions that would raise to see that first, and then on the basis of our experience until then to see whether we could find a solution which would take less time in court. So I do agree with you that you reminded me in very gentle words, I remember, that we failed to give a decision. We then gave a decision that we would not allow the marking to be done in court, but the Chamber had considered, by itself, that they would first like to have experience with a couple of these maps and then see whether perhaps the additional markings could be made out of the specific court time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, you just said that the decision was that you would not allow the marking to be done in court; I assume you meant out of court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Out of court, yes, it was a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note that the other map which the witness had prepared out of court, and indeed with the assistance of others, was not the subject of any objection by the Defence, which clearly inconsistent with the position they took in relation to the marking of the front line positions. I simply make this point to emphasise that we have done and continue to do our best to live within the date we are required to complete our case. In doing that, we have to clearly make -- anticipate what decisions will be made by the Trial Chamber, such as these in relation to the tender of material. If the Defence is given four hours of cross-examination and perhaps more on the basis that your calculations indicate that we took four hours in chief, and much of that time was occupied in doing a task which it transpires, having regard to the inconsistency of the Defence position, perhaps could have been reduced to two hours or two and a half hours or three hours, then, as has happened, we are left in an embarrassing situation in terms of completing our case. Mr. President, perhaps tomorrow I could have the opportunity of addressing the Trial Chamber as to where the Prosecution presently stands, given the timetable, and the 92 bis decision, which we have not received but which you have indicated the important aspects in terms of us preparing our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think the whole disposition is known to you. If we are not able to deliver the decision in writing this afternoon, if there are any further details necessary, the Chamber will give them. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The Defence is even more concerned to save time than the Prosecution. And we can start tomorrow morning right away. Since Mr. Ierace would like to address the court about something, we would like to know what is happening with the documents which I said are either falsified or tampered with. This is important for us because we have to be organised ourselves and the Prosecution provides documents to us and to you and the documents on those dates are not quite right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I invited the Prosecution to respond at shortest notice on your observations. The Chamber will see what that response is and then will give a decision. We will adjourn until tomorrow morning --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before we do, I think I invited the Defence to state a position in writing and we could respond and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. I asked to put the proposals in writing in one page or less, I remember that I said. So just very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have already done that. We did that last night between midnight and 2.00 a.m., and this is probably already somewhere in the Registry and the Prosecution should have that by now. But I can provide the Prosecution with a copy, if somebody would follow me to the Defence attorneys' room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then we will receive on short notice the response of the Prosecution. We will then adjourn until tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Maybe this is of assistance for the Prosecutor, but today, on page 3, line 19 says that the president says, "I take it that the Prosecution will respond in due course." It doesn't say in the written form, but as far as I understood, it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That was yesterday, Your Honour, that we were required to do it in writing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's deal with the matter as soon as possible and not spend too much time on things that do not really come to the core of the problem. I now give it a last try that we will adjourn until 9.00 tomorrow morning and I hope that everyone has an opportunity to sleep in the late evening or early night hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
